# The First Three NIST Post-Quantum Standards Serve Two Purposes

In August 2024, the Secretary of Commerce approved FIPS 203, FIPS 204 and FIPS 205. The standards specify schemes for two distinct purposes: establishing a shared secret and creating digital signatures.

FIPS 203 specifies ML-KEM, which establishes a shared secret between parties communicating over a public channel. FIPS 204 specifies a module-lattice-based digital signature scheme, while FIPS 205 specifies a stateless hash-based digital signature scheme.

The schemes are designed to resist future quantum attacks.
